title: The New Stew
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'ew' (the /oo/ sound as in new, stew and chew)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'ew' — another way to write the /oo/ sound your child knows from 'moon', used in new, stew, chew and few.

pages.illustration: Nell the bee beside a brand new cooking pot, gleaming and far too big for her, admiring her reflection in it. Bright and proud.
Nell perched on the pot's rim stirring with a long twig, steam rising past her. Warm kitchen-ish light, rich browns.

pages.text: Fig blew on the hot stew.
pages.illustration: Fig the caterpillar blowing hard across a spoonful of stew, cheeks out, steam bending away from him. Comic effort.

pages.text: It was too hot to chew.
pages.illustration: Fig recoiling with his mouth open and tongue out, one leg fanning his face. The stew clearly far too hot.

pages.text: The stew had a few peas.
pages.illustration: Close on the surface of the stew with exactly a few round green peas floating in it, drawn countably. Rich and appetising.

pages.text: Nell had a big cup too.
pages.illustration: Nell with an enormous cup, drinking with both front legs round it, almost disappearing behind it. Funny scale.
Both of them sitting on the pot rim with full bowls, eyes shut in appreciation. Warm and companionable.

pages.text: Fig and Nell had it all up.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the pot scraped completely clean and gleaming, two very round friends asleep against it. Cosy evening light.
